Planning guidelines, not medical advice. The limits are not universal human limits. Overlapping time counts once.

Focus has run for more than %1$d min without a break. Try 10–15 minutes of quiet rest.
Lessons and study together exceed %1$d min without at least 20 min of restorative rest. Plan movement or screen-free rest.
After lessons, leave at least %1$d min before studying for a meal and a mental transition.
Daily focus exceeds your limit of %1$d min. Consider shortening or moving some work; a break alone does not reduce the amount of study.
Sitting work has lasted more than %1$d min. Stand up, look into the distance or take a short walk.
There is %1$d–%2$d min of unscheduled time during study. Merge the blocks or turn the gap into deliberate rest.
%1$d min of rest added. Lessons and other commitments were not moved.
Focus is split by %1$d min of rest; study time is preserved.
Focus moved for a safe transition; %1$d min of rest added.
A break is already planned or the warning no longer applies.
There is not enough safe room for a break. Shorten or move the block; the timetable is unchanged.
A tap inserts rest into free time or safely splits focus. Lessons, exams and personal commitments are never moved.
An end before the start means it continues into the next day.
From the chosen date on, on the marked days.
This date only; the weekly blueprint stays unchanged.
A few taps. Everything stays on this device.
Every subject automatically gets presets for lessons, study and exams.
Add a subject. Presets for lessons, study and exams become available right away.
One tap saves the exam for the date and time already selected. We never guess a date.
A deadline is a marker with no duration and no block reminder. Add a separate study block to prepare.
An end before the start means the next day. Start and end must differ.
Changes every week, including past ones. Existing exceptions for single dates stay.
Changes only this occurrence; the other weeks stay as they are.
Six digits, e.g. 4F8CFF. An empty field means a colour from the shelf.
The routine “%1$s” will be deleted in every week, together with its exceptions and history. For a single day use “Skip this day”.
The entry “%1$s” will be permanently deleted from this device.
Blocks and deadlines stay. Only the link to the subject, its colour and its default duration are removed.
The grid scrolls sideways. Tapping a day or a block opens the day view.
A stronger colour means more planned focus. Days of rest count too.
%1$s: %2$d minutes of focus, %3$d exams and %4$d deadlines.

Choose the end of teaching for this school year in settings.
Year 3: 24 June 2027. Final year: 21 May 2027. You can adjust the date for your school.
No holidays are included for this school year.
How densely deadlines fall over the next eight weeks; includes your exams, IAs, EE and TOK.
No deadlines yet. Add exam, IA, EE and TOK dates once your school confirms them.
No connection. No account, network, analytics or cloud backup.
Removing the app or clearing its storage permanently deletes the timetable.
Notifications are off. Planning works without them too.
Access to exact alarms is granted.
Exact alarms are not allowed. Fallback reminders are approximate and may be late.
Silent, low-priority notifications. The system Do Not Disturb mode stays untouched.
The window applies every day, weekends included. An earlier end time means it runs past midnight. Android decides whether a banner appears; quiet notifications usually wait in the notification shade.
Different feedback for a tap, a drag, a finished task and a warning. It also respects the system vibration setting.
Sound on confirmations, deletions and panels opening, matched to the haptics. Volume follows the system media volume; switching it on plays a preview.
Countdown to the end of teaching
The Western calendar for 2026/27 is included. We do not guess or download other years.
Year 3: 2027-06-24. Final years: 2027-05-21. An IB school may set a different date. The countdown itself never cancels routine blocks.

20 minutes of real rest or free time resets mental load; 5 minutes resets a sitting streak. Rest that overlaps work does not count. Work already done stays in the calculation. These are planning guidelines, not a health assessment.
The limits and switches apply to the warnings shown and the breaks suggested. Save your changes together.
No foreground service and no polling loop. Android can delay even an exact alarm while the phone is idle or restricted. After a force stop, open the app again.
An optional sample of subjects, an IB week and deadlines. Not an official school timetable. Nothing of it loads on first start.
Sample subjects, blocks and unofficial 2026/27 deadlines will be added. Existing data stays. Reminders in the sample are switched off. The sample loads only once.
The sample is loaded; every sample reminder is off.

A delay is a normal part of the day. We use spare room and reserves first; fixed commitments stay put.
The plan is adjusted: %1$d min of room · in the queue: %2$d.
Nothing is waiting in the queue.
The task has a new slot.
There is not enough free room that day. The task stays safely stored.
Mid-afternoon: room for an easier rhythm
These are adjustable mathematical heuristics, not a measurement of your body clock and not medical advice.
How long did you actually spend?
Your confirmation improves future plans. When you started the timer we use the start and end times; we never track activity in the background.
A fixed block is never moved, shortened or postponed.
More elasticity means more willingness to shorten. Rest and fixed commitments are never shortened automatically.
Check the minimum, the elasticity and the importance. The minimum cannot exceed the duration.
We schedule the preparation backwards into smaller blocks and add a shared reserve. No sample estimates are inserted.
%1$d min of preparation planned · %2$d min in the queue.
The estimate should be between 0 and 1000 hours.
Add an hour estimate in the deadline editor.
Link to an exam or deadline
The gaps widen as you go. Revisions use at most 20% of your daily study capacity; we pick the quieter day inside the allowed window.
Check the title and dates (at most 366 days), 1–52 revisions and 1–120 minutes.
Revisions planned: %1$d · %2$d min in the queue.
Remove the topic and its revisions?
The planned blocks for this topic and its queue entry will be deleted. Other subjects and deadlines stay.
Centre of the afternoon dip · HH:mm
Check the time window and the allowed minutes.
At most 270 min of independent study; focus 25–90 min; at least 45 min of rest after lessons. Revisions get at most a fifth of the real daily capacity.
A fixed commitment is here. The timer is stopped; save the work you have done.
When you start work yourself, we adjust the following flexible blocks once you run over. It works with the app open and when you return to it, with no background service.
The preparation is already scheduled. The existing plan was not duplicated.
There is currently no room for %1$d min of safety reserve. The plan therefore lacks part of the protection it intended.
The chosen date is after the linked deadline. The task stays in the queue.
Schedule the earlier preparation stage first.
The time spent will not be saved as completed work. The timetable adjusted so far stays unchanged.
Finish the work or stop the timer of this block first.
Finish the previous preparation stage first.
This time belongs to a fixed commitment or protected rest.
The system clock changed. Check and confirm the actual minutes by hand.
Changing the start keeps the %1$d min duration. You can also correct the end by hand.
Add a break after the lesson
The break follows the end of the lesson. It does not run when the lesson is cancelled or during holidays; an overlap does not count as rest. Its reminder is off by default.
Choose 1 to 60 minutes for the break.
The break is already covered or overlaps a commitment.

This is planned, protected time — not a sleep measurement and not an alarm clock. The automatic planner never puts study inside it.
Different at the weekend (Saturday and Sunday)

Copy the timetable rows from your school’s site (e.g. ManageBac) and paste them here. I recognise shapes like “Mon 08:00–08:50 Maths” and “Monday 8:00-8:50 Math”; each row becomes a weekly lesson block without a reminder.
A one-off import of a timetable copied from ManageBac. Nothing goes to the cloud — the timetable stays your local setting.
I could not recognise any lesson — every row needs a day, a range (e.g. 08:00–08:50) and a subject name.
Timetable imported — the weekly lesson blocks are ready
If the waking time is earlier on the clock than bedtime, it means the next day. For example Sunday 23:00 → Monday 07:00.
An optional calm start after waking. 0 means no extra block.
The rhythm is saved. A night already begun is not changed; the new times apply from the next bedtime.
Check for two different times, at least one day, and 0–120 minutes of morning transition.
Applies to new subjects and to lessons without a chosen subject. Saved subjects keep their own default duration.
Insert a short break every N minutes of focused work.
Breaks are suggested only where no natural rest already exists (lunch, a free period or a longer break). The last part of a block is not marked.
A short list of what went wrong. It stays in memory, travels nowhere, and helps you say what happened instead of guessing.
Export the timetable into a JSON file you can import back at any time. An AI can also prepare a matching file from a photo of your school timetable.
Copy the JSON to the clipboard and save it or send it to an AI for editing.
Paste JSON here (for example one an AI built from a timetable photo) and import it.
